# Saving pictures

@difference Extension: [SaveBuffer](SaveBuffer), [SaveImage](SaveImage) and the new [SaveTexture](SaveTexture) write PNG, JPEG, WebP, JPEG XL, TGA, DDS and BMP files with settings, mark them as made by the program, and can encode on another thread with [AsyncSaving](AsyncSaving).

The original [SaveBuffer](SaveBuffer) and [SaveImage](SaveImage) only wrote BMP files, whatever the name of the file was. Here the end of the file name picks the format, and an optional last argument, a text of settings, picks how the file is made. Old calls work as before, except that a name that ends in `.png` has been a PNG since the early versions, and the other endings below are new.

| Ending | Format | Settings that count | Metadata |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `.bmp`, or any other ending | BMP, 32 bit with alpha | none | none |
| `.png` | PNG, with an alpha channel only if a pixel is see-through | `compression` | Exif (`eXIf` chunk) and a `Software` text |
| `.jpg`, `.jpeg` | JPEG, baseline or progressive (no alpha) | `quality`, `subsampling`, `progressive` | Exif (`APP1` segment) |
| `.webp` | WebP, lossy or lossless | `quality`, `lossless` | Exif (`EXIF` chunk) |
| `.jxl` | JPEG XL, lossy or lossless | `quality`, `distance`, `lossless`, `effort` | Exif (`Exif` box) |
| `.tga` | TGA | `rle` | none |
| `.dds` | DDS, uncompressed or block compressed (BC1 to BC5, BC7), with or without mip maps | `format`, `mipmaps`, `levels`, `srgb` | none |
| `.avif` | not written, the result is 0 | | |

AVIF can be read but not written: the AV1 encoder is the biggest part of an AVIF library and would about double the size of every program, which is why it is left out of the build. Convert to WebP or JPEG XL instead.

The same 640x360 screenshot (921,738 bytes as BMP), cut to the area that shows the differences and saved with different settings, then loaded again. Lossless files are the same as the original, the lossy ones lose detail where it is sharp (JPEG at quality 40 shows blocks and smeared colors):

![The same picture saved as PNG, JPEG, WebP and JPEG XL with different settings](media/saving/formats.png)

## Settings

The settings are one text of `name=value` pairs, separated by commas, semicolons or spaces. Names are not case sensitive, and a name without a value (`progressive`) means `=1`. A setting that the format of the file does not use is ignored, so one text can be used for several files. A name that does not exist or a value that is not allowed is reported once on the console and ignored, the rest still counts.

| Setting | Values | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `quality` | 0 to 100 | 90 | JPEG, WebP (lossy) and JPEG XL (lossy): higher is better and bigger. JPEG XL turns it into a distance the way `cjxl` does, and 100 is lossless. |
| `subsampling` | `444`, `422`, `420` (also `4:2:0`) | `420` | JPEG: how much of the color is kept. `444` keeps all of it (sharp colored edges, big files), `420` a quarter. |
| `progressive` | 0 or 1 | 0 | JPEG: the file is made of scans that show the whole picture blurry first and sharpen it, which viewers show while a file is still loading. |
| `lossless` | 0 or 1 | 0 | WebP and JPEG XL: no loss at all. For JPEG XL `lossless=0` keeps it lossy even at `quality=100`. |
| `distance` | 0 to 25 | from `quality` | JPEG XL: the lossy distance directly, 1 is visually lossless and 0 is lossless. Wins over `quality`. |
| `effort` | 1 to 9 | 5 | JPEG XL: how long the encoder searches. 1 is fastest, 9 gives the smallest files. |
| `compression` | 0 to 9 | 6 | PNG: 0 stores the pixels without compression, 1 is the fastest and 9 the smallest file. |
| `rle` | 0 or 1 | 1 | TGA: run length encoding. |
| `format` | `rgba8`, `bgra8`, `bgr8`, `rgb565`, `r8`, `rg8`, `bc1` (`dxt1`), `bc2` (`dxt3`), `bc3` (`dxt5`), `bc4`, `bc5`, `bc7` | `rgba8` | DDS: how the pixels are stored. `r8`, `bc4` keep red, `rg8`, `bc5` red and green; the others keep all colors, and the formats with alpha (`rgba8`, `bgra8`, `bc2`, `bc3`, `bc7`) keep that too (`bc1` has a hole for pixels that are mostly see-through). |
| `mipmaps` | 0 or 1 | 0 | DDS: store all mip maps down to 1x1, each made by averaging 2x2 pixels of the one before. |
| `levels` | 1 to 16 | 1 | DDS: store at most this many levels (the picture itself is the first), so `levels=3` is a picture and two smaller ones. It wins over `mipmaps`. |
| `srgb` | 0 or 1 | 0 | DDS: mark the colors as sRGB, which needs a DX10 header (`bgr8` becomes `bgra8`). `rgb565`, `r8`, `rg8`, `bc4` and `bc5` have no sRGB form. |
| `metadata` | 0 or 1 | 1 | Whether the file says which program made it. |

```blitzbasic
SaveBuffer FrontBuffer(), "shot.png"                                   ; lossless, default compression
SaveBuffer FrontBuffer(), "shot.jpg", "quality=95,subsampling=444"      ; sharp colors
SaveBuffer FrontBuffer(), "web.jpg", "quality=70,progressive=1"         ; small, shows blurry first
SaveBuffer FrontBuffer(), "shot.webp", "lossless=1"
SaveBuffer FrontBuffer(), "shot.jxl", "distance=1,effort=7"             ; visually lossless
SaveBuffer FrontBuffer(), "plain.png", "metadata=0, compression=9"
```

## DDS files

`format` picks what is stored, and the others only add to it. Uncompressed formats keep every pixel as it is (`rgb565` loses the low bits), the block compressed ones cut the picture into 4x4 pixel blocks of 8 or 16 bytes, which is 4 to 8 times smaller than `rgba8` and loses some detail where a block has many different colors. They stay compressed on the graphics card when the file is loaded again with [LoadTexture](LoadTexture). `bc7` is written in its mode 6 only (one pair of RGBA ends for the block), which fits blocks with a smooth change of color and alpha best, and is not as good as an encoder that tries every mode; it is meant for quick exports, and sizes of a picture that are not a multiple of 4 repeat the edge pixels inside the last blocks.

Files that older programs can read use the plain header (`DXT1`, `DXT3`, `DXT5`, `BC4U`, `BC5U` and masks for the uncompressed ones). A DX10 header is written where there is no other way: `bc7`, `rg8` and `srgb=1`.

```blitzbasic
SaveImage img, "sprite.dds"                                  ; RGBA8, no loss
SaveImage img, "sprite.dds", 0, "format=bc3, mipmaps=1"      ; small, with mip maps
SaveTexture tex, "albedo.dds", 0, "format=bc7, srgb=1, mipmaps"
SaveBuffer ImageBuffer(img), "mask.dds", "format=bc4"        ; red channel only
```

## Metadata

Files carry Exif metadata with the description and the software set to `Generated by <title>`, where the title is the one of [AppTitle](AppTitle) and `BlitzLLVM` until the program sets one. PNG files have it as `eXIf` chunk and as a `Software` text chunk too, because some programs only read the text. JPEG, WebP and JPEG XL files have the Exif block that image viewers show as the camera/software information. BMP, TGA and DDS have no place for it. `metadata=0` leaves it out.

## On another thread

Encoding takes time that a game may not have in a frame. On a test machine a 1920x1080 screenshot took about 60 ms as JPEG, 80 ms to 2 seconds as PNG (`compression=1` to `9`), 165 ms as lossy WebP and 80 ms to 3 seconds as JPEG XL (`effort=3` to a lossless `effort=7`). [AsyncSaving](AsyncSaving) `True` (or `BLITZLLVM_ASYNC_SAVE=1` in the environment) makes the save commands only read the pixels, and a worker thread encodes and writes the file. [SavesPending](SavesPending) and [SavesFailed](SavesFailed) tell how it is going, and a program that ends waits for its saves. It is off by default, so a save has written its file when the command returns.

## Libraries

The WebP and JPEG XL files are written by the same shared libraries that read them (`libwebp`, `libjxl`) next to the program, which are looked up when the first such file is saved. If one is missing the save gives 0 and the console says so once.
